observation: Fresh main validates durable event and evidence identity, yet generic update() could still replace both arrays with structurally valid forged ledgers. That bypassed the existing dedicated writers: eventObject() owns event sequence/time/type and addEvidence() owns evidence id/time.
changes: Reject generic update patches containing events so event history continues to flow through eventObject().
Reject generic update patches containing evidence so evidence identity continues to flow through addEvidence().
Keep dedicated event/evidence append paths and ordinary mission updates unchanged, with focused regression coverage.

verification.pre_fix_source_contract_replay: EXPECTED FAIL: a structurally valid replacement events/evidence array passed candidate shape validation and was persisted before the update event append.
verification.post_fix_contract_replay: PASS: generic ledger replacement is rejected before mutation while addEvidence() and ordinary update() still append through their dedicated writers.
verification.focused_regression_contract: tests/autonomous-mission-owned-ledger-write-integrity.test.mjs covers rejected replacements, durable non-mutation, and normal dedicated append paths.

truth_boundary: This cycle establishes write-path ownership already implied by dedicated writers. It does not cryptographically authenticate persisted ledgers and does not prevent an external actor from consistently rewriting the whole mission file.
